newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-FRENCH QUALIFIER GOLMARD UPSETS FERRERA.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-FRENCH QUALIFIER GOLMARD UPSETS FERRERA.

text.p: French qualifer Jerome Golmard upset second seeded Wayne Ferreira of South Africa 4-6 6-3 6-2 in the first round of the $328,000 Arizona Classic tennis tournament on Monday.
Third-seed and Australian Open finalist Carlos Moya of Spain edged Mikael Tillstrom of Sweden 3-6 6-2 7-6 (7-2).
In another surprise, American Bryan Shelton upended injured fellow-countryman MaliVai Washington 3-6 7-5 6-2.
It was Goldmar's second career victory in three attempts over the ninth ranked Ferreira and his best result over a Top 10 player.
"I'm so happy," said Golmard. "I served very well and I had not too much pressure.
After splitting sets, the Frenchman took control with a key break to start the third set. He built it to 5-2 before the lefthander rifled his third ace to compete the 1-hour, 32-minute upset.
"I thought I could win the match when I did the break in the first game of the last set," said Goldmar, 24. "I said if I serve very good then I win. I am so happy."

The 192nd-ranked Shelton, 31, failed to qualify for the main singles but gained entry as a "lucky loser" when Patrick McEnroe withdrew with a recurring right shoulder injury shortly before the evening match.
A lucky loser is the highest ranked player who lost in the last round of qualifying.
"Pretty lucky, huh," said Shelton. "I found out 40 minutes before the match. You can't pass up an opportunity to play."
"I forget to ask who I play until five minutes before I got on the court," he said. "My mind was all over the court. I said, 'Wow, I'm playing.' I didn't think I would be playing singles this week."
Shelton dropped the opening set and was two points away from a quick exit as Washington served at 5-4 30-30.
But the seventh seed failed to close out the match, and a recurring left knee injury from a recent Davis Cup match last month begain to pain him.

"It felt OK in the first set then it got worse from the second set on," said Washington of the inflamed left knee that limited his movement. "If I could've held that game, I could've been in the trainer's room getting treatment and everything could've been fine."
With Washington hobbling, Shelton took control of the one-hour, 37-minute match against his longtime friend.
"Mal isn't 100 percent right now. I think his knee is still bothering him. He definitely wasn't moving like he normally does.
Moya, 20, took advantage of Tillstrom's poor play to dominate the decisive third set tiebreaker.
"I think I played well and he made two double faults," said Moya, the world's No. 10 ranked player, who improved to 13-3 on the year. "That's pretty much what decided the match."
